verdict.rationale: vLLM's own docs name PagedAttention as its mechanism for efficiently managing attention key/value memory, and community users confirm they rely on vLLM's KV cache, so the core paged KV-cache capability is first-party. The evidence pack contains only one-line feature mentions, though, and none of it documents the outcomes the story asks for: higher concurrent request capacity and freedom from memory fragmentation. missing for 10: documentation that paged KV management eliminates or reduces memory fragmentation, evidence that it increases concurrent request capacity or batch size, in-depth first-party docs on the PagedAttention block/paging mechanism, independent benchmarks corroborating memory-efficiency gains.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on paged memory management for attention key/value cache to maximize concurrent request capacity without memory fragmentation
